parsed.brief_reason: The patch correctly fixes the off-by-one error in the boundary condition. The original code used `charno < sourceExcerpt.length()` which excluded the case where an error occurs at the end of a line (charno equals length), but the tests expect the caret to be displayed in that case. Changing to `charno <= sourceExcerpt.length()` is minimal, general, and aligns with the comment indicating that charno == sourceExcerpt.length() is a valid scenario. The only minor concern is that the loop `for (int i = 0; i < charno; i++)` will access `sourceExcerpt.charAt(i)` up to index charno-1, which is safe when charno equals length, but the logic relies on this boundary behavior being intentional.
